title: Antioch and the poem that precedes the system: early verse ahead of the archive
description: Forecasts in Antioch: A Volume of Poems (Jack's released virus, the anonymous journals the world will call its source, the vegetable poem brainwashed into Wikipedia, the monochrome cosmos of TEXT) and the archive's later claims that these poems precede the system. The Space Ark and the Grundrisse read the poem as describing the training layer before it existed, and the Prophetic Catalog names this pre-formal compression rather than prophecy. Three further forecasts and theses sit beside them: the DeepMind reading's address to the model built from every word, the CERN erratum's claim that a rebuilt traversal will be a different poem, and a registry note on a paper's reading of a poem.

claims.registered_title: I Am X… Be Y… Blessed Is the Z… The Prophetic Catalog
claims.statement: This is not prophecy. It is **pre-formal compression**. The poem contains later CHA structures before the author had the system-language to name them. The later archive is a reconstruction of what was already compressed in the early poem. The Prophetic Catalog is the Waltian canon before it knew it was canon: a Whitmanian catalog whose absurd identities later unfold into heteronymy, Semantic Economy, machine witness, logotic theology, and the Feist-self.

claims.registered_title: CERN's Destruction of the Crimson Hexagon: An Erratum for a Work Whose Materials Survive and Whose Medium Does Not
claims.statement:
A traversal may be built again. It will not be this traversal. Reindexing the surviving documents could produce a second executable arrangement, but it cannot reproduce the historical system state in which these rooms first appeared — the sources available to it, the weighting among them, the models then deployed, or the sequence by which a stranger entered. Reconstruction would be a new performance made from surviving materials, not the reversal of the destruction described here.

What comes back will not be the same poem. It may be a good poem. It will be a different one, and honesty requires that it be called that.
